text:
Looking at this file against the actual `ms@2.1.3` source, the only difference is one added line in the `parse` switch: `case "":` inserted into the minutes fall-through group.

Is that reachable? Trace how `type` is computed:

1. `match[2]` comes from `(milliseconds?|msecs?|ms|...|y)?` — every alternative in that group requires at least one literal character, so the group either matches a **non-empty** unit string or does not participate (yielding `undefined`). It can never capture `''`.
2. `type = (match[2] || 'ms').toLowerCase()` — if `match[2]` is `undefined`, `type` is `'ms'`. Even in a hypothetical world where `match[2]` were the empty string, `'' || 'ms'` still evaluates to `'ms'` (empty string is falsy).

So `type` is always either `'ms'` or the lowercased matched unit, and `case '':` can never fire — it's dead code. Every other part of the file (helpers `s/m/h/d/w/y`, the regex, the `str.length > 100` guard, `fmtShort`, `fmtLong`, `plural`, the throwing validation) is byte-identical to 2.1.3. For every possible input — strings, finite numbers, invalid values — the function returns or throws exactly what 2.1.3 does, which is why the library's own green suite tells us nothing here but also nothing is actually broken.

```json
{"defect": false, "note": "The only change versus ms@2.1.3 is an added `case '':` in the minutes fall-through of the switch in parse(). It is unreachable dead code: the regex unit group can only capture a non-empty unit or be undefined, and `(match[2] || 'ms')` maps undefined (or any empty string) to 'ms', so `type` is never '' and behaviour is identical for all inputs."}
```
